title: Twisted-arrow site presentation of internal group actions on module sheaves
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(C,J)$ be a $\mathcal V$-small site with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $K:C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Grp}$ be a sheaf of groups with $\mathcal V$-small values. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative unital rings on $C$, with $\mathcal V$-small values. Give $R$ the trivial $K$-action. A $K$-equivariant $R$-module sheaf is a sheaf of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with natural operations $K(U)\times M(U)\to M(U)$ satisfying the group-action laws and linearity in $M(U)$; morphisms commute with these operations.

Define $C_K$ to have the objects of $C$, arrows $(f,a):V\to U$ with $f:V\to U$ in $C$ and $a\in K(V)$, identities $(1,1)$, and composition
$$(f,a)\circ(g,b)=(f\circ g,b\,g^*a).$$
Use the covering families $\{(f_i,a_i):U_i\to U\}$ for which $\{f_i:U_i\to U\}$ is a $J$-covering family. These families make $C_K$ a small site. The presheaf $R_K$ given by $R_K(U)=R(U)$ and $R_K(f,a)=f^*$ is a sheaf of commutative rings on this site. There is an additive equivalence from $K$-equivariant $R$-module sheaves to $\operatorname{Mod}(R_K)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] sending $M$ to the same section modules with restriction $m\mapsto a\cdot f^*m$ along $(f,a)$; its inverse restricts to $(f,1)$ and recovers $a\cdot m$ from $(1_U,a)$.

For an equivariant presheaf of $R$-modules, restriction to the arrows $(f,1)$ identifies its module sheafification on $C_K$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] with its module sheafification on $C$, with the induced $K$-action. In particular, forgetting the $K$-action creates kernels and cokernels: the underlying kernel is the sectionwise kernel and the underlying cokernel is the sheafification on $C$ of the sectionwise cokernel. A module sheaf on $C_K$ is zero if and only if its restriction to $C$ is zero.
